segments.text: When Maya joined her school's environmental club, she expected to spend weekends cleaning the local river. Instead, the first meeting was spent looking at a pile of lunch boxes.
The club had noticed that students threw away hundreds of plastic containers every week.
segments.translation: 社团注意到，学生们每周都会扔掉数百个塑料餐盒。

segments.text: They wanted to find a practical way to reduce the waste.

Their first idea was to ask everyone to bring a reusable box from home. However, many students forgot theirs, and some worried that washing a box after lunch would take too much time. Maya suggested a different plan: the school could lend out clean containers and collect them at the end of the day. The club tested the idea in one classroom for two weeks. Students paid a small deposit, which they got back when they returned a container.

The trial was not perfect. A few containers went missing, and the volunteers had to spend time washing them. Still, the amount of plastic rubbish from that classroom fell by nearly half. More importantly, students began discussing other ways to cut waste, such as sharing books and using both sides of paper. The school later expanded the lending system to the whole building.
Maya learned that changing a habit does not always require a big speech or a strict rule.
A solution is more likely to work when it fits into people's daily lives.
segments.translation: 当一种解决方案融入人们的日常生活时，它更有可能奏效。

segments.text: Small steps can also help people see that their choices matter, making them willing to try the next one.
segments.translation: 小小的行动也能让人们看到自己的选择很重要，从而愿意尝试下一步。

questions.stem: Why did the environmental club first discuss lunch boxes?
options: They wanted to raise money by selling boxes.
They noticed a large amount of plastic waste from them.
Students had asked for a longer lunch break.
The river cleanup had been cancelled.
questions.explanation: The club began with a problem they could observe at school: disposable lunch containers were creating a lot of waste.
questions.evidence: The club had noticed that students threw away hundreds of plastic containers every week.
optionExplanations: 无中生有：文章没有提到售卖饭盒或筹款。
正确：对应每周产生大量塑料饭盒垃圾这一发现。
无中生有：午休时长与讨论无关。
偷换话题：文章开头提到周末清理河流只是 Maya 的预期，并未说活动取消。

questions.stem: What made the club's lending plan more practical for students?
options: Students could borrow a clean container and get their deposit back.
Students no longer had to eat lunch at school.
The school gave every student a new box to keep.
Volunteers delivered lunch to each classroom.
questions.explanation: The school would lend clean containers, and returning one meant students got their small deposit back. This addressed the problems of forgetting a box and not wanting to wash it.
questions.evidence: the school could lend out clean containers and collect them at the end of the day.
optionExplanations: 正确：借用和退还押金让学生更容易参与，也减少了自带和清洗的麻烦。
无中生有：文章没有说学生不在学校吃饭。
偷换概念：饭盒是借用后归还，不是发给学生永久保留。
无中生有：没有志愿者送餐的安排。

questions.stem: What is the main lesson Maya learned?
options: Rules are the only way to change people's habits.
Environmental projects should begin with a large campaign.
A solution that fits daily life can encourage lasting change.
Students should focus on one problem and ignore the rest.
questions.explanation: Maya concludes that practical solutions fit people's routines, and small successes can motivate them to make further changes.
questions.evidence: A solution is more likely to work when it fits into people's daily lives. Small steps can also help people see that their choices matter, making them willing to try the next one.
optionExplanations: 与原文相反：Maya 认为不一定需要严格规定。
无中生有：文章强调小步骤，并未要求大型宣传活动。
正确：概括了方案贴近日常生活、小行动带来后续改变的观点。
偷换概念：文章举出减少纸张等后续行动，鼓励继续改善。

title: How Sea Otters Help Kelp Forests

segments.text: Along the Pacific coast, kelp forests provide food and shelter for many sea animals. But these underwater forests face a serious threat: sea urchins. When too many urchins eat young kelp, large areas of the sea floor can become almost empty.
Sea otters help keep this balance by eating the urchins, and researchers have found that places with more otters often have healthier kelp forests.
segments.translation: 海獭通过捕食海胆帮助维持生态平衡；研究人员发现，海獭较多的地方往往拥有更健康的海带森林。

segments.text: For a long time, scientists thought the story was simple: more otters meant more kelp. Recent studies, however, suggest that the relationship is more complex. Otters do not eat the same amount every day, and storms, water temperature, and human activity can also affect kelp growth. In some areas, even a small number of otters can make a difference because they hunt in places where urchins are especially active.
The animals' influence can therefore be much greater than their numbers alone might suggest.
segments.translation: 因此，这些动物的影响可能远超单看它们的数量所能推测的程度。

segments.text: This finding matters to people who want to protect coastal environments. Simply bringing otters back may not solve every problem, but understanding where they feed can help conservation teams choose which places need attention first. It can also remind local communities that protecting one species may support many others.
A healthy ecosystem depends not on a single animal, but on the connections among living things and the conditions around them.
segments.translation: 健康的生态系统并非只依赖某一种动物，而是取决于生物之间的联系以及周围环境条件。

questions.stem: How do sea otters help kelp forests?
options: They protect young kelp from storms.
They eat sea urchins that feed on kelp.
They make the water warmer for kelp to grow.
They move kelp to areas with fewer animals.
questions.explanation: Sea urchins eat young kelp, and sea otters help control the urchin population by eating them.
questions.evidence: Sea otters help keep this balance by eating the urchins, and researchers have found that places with more otters often have healthier kelp forests.
optionExplanations: 无中生有：文章没有说海獭能保护海带免受风暴影响。
正确：海獭捕食会吃海带的海胆。
无中生有：文章没有提到海獭改变水温。
无中生有：文章没有说海獭搬运海带。

questions.stem: Why might a small number of sea otters still have a strong effect in some areas?
options: They eat urchins in places where the urchins are especially active.
They stop people from entering the water.
They produce more kelp than larger groups do.
They prevent all storms from reaching the coast.
questions.explanation: The passage says that otters may have a strong influence when they hunt in areas with especially active urchins.
questions.evidence: In some areas, even a small number of otters can make a difference because they hunt in places where urchins are especially active.
optionExplanations: 正确：捕食集中在海胆活跃区域，因此少量海獭也可能产生明显影响。
无中生有：文章没有提到限制人们下水。
偷换概念：海獭捕食海胆，不会生产海带。
过度推断：文章没有说海獭可以阻挡风暴。

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Sea otters are the only animals needed to protect the coast.
Kelp forests grow best when people stay away from the sea.
Sea otters can support kelp forests, but ecosystem health depends on several connected factors.
Scientists have already solved every problem facing kelp forests.
questions.explanation: The passage explains the helpful role of otters while emphasizing that kelp forests are affected by several environmental factors and relationships.
questions.evidence: A healthy ecosystem depends not on a single animal, but on the connections among living things and the conditions around them.
optionExplanations: 与原文相反：文章明确指出生态系统不依赖单一物种。
无中生有：文章没有提出人类远离海边就能解决问题。
正确：概括了海獭的作用以及生态系统的多因素关系。
无中生有：文章讨论研究发现和保护方向，没有说问题已经解决。

title: A Library Built One Book at a Time

segments.text: After college, Mei returned to her mountain village and found the community room filled with unused chairs. Younger children had few chances to read outside school, so she wondered whether the room could become a library.
She began with a simple request: each family could give one book it no longer needed.
segments.translation: 她从一个简单的请求开始：每户人家都可以捐出一本不再需要的书。

segments.text: The first collection was small, and some books were too difficult for young readers. A retired teacher sorted the books by age and topic. A carpenter repaired the shelves, while children made signs. Mei kept a borrowing notebook so families could track each book.
By giving each person a clear role, she turned the project from her private idea into a shared effort.
segments.translation: 她为每个人安排了明确的角色，使这个项目从她个人的想法变成了大家共同的努力。

segments.text: The library did not become popular overnight. During the first month, few children visited. Mei then invited them to read aloud on Saturdays and recommend books to one another. Gradually, parents stopped by after work, and older students helped younger ones read.
The room became more than a place to borrow books; it became a place where neighbors met and learned together.
segments.translation: 这个房间不再只是借书的地方，也成了邻里相聚、共同学习的场所。

segments.text: Mei says the most important change was not the number of books, but the feeling that people could improve their village together. The library still depends on volunteers and has a modest collection. Yet it shows that a useful community space does not always need a large budget. Sometimes it begins with an open room, a shared idea, and people willing to help.

questions.stem: How did the village first begin collecting books for the library?
options: A school bought a large collection for the village.
Mei asked each family to donate one unwanted book.
Children borrowed books from the town library.
The carpenter exchanged shelves for books.
questions.explanation: Mei started the collection by asking each family to give one book it no longer needed.
questions.evidence: She began with a simple request: each family could give one book it no longer needed.
optionExplanations: 无中生有：文章没有提到学校购买书籍。
正确：对应 Mei 向每户人家征集一本闲置书的做法。
偷换概念：文章提到的是村里的孩子缺少课外阅读机会，并非从镇图书馆借书。
无中生有：木匠修理了书架，没有用书交换。

questions.stem: Why did Mei invite children to read aloud and recommend books?
options: To help more people become interested in visiting the library.
To make children return every book on the same day.
To replace the retired teacher's work.
To keep parents from entering the room.
questions.explanation: Few children visited at first. Reading aloud and sharing recommendations helped make the library more welcoming and attractive.
questions.evidence: Mei then invited them to read aloud on Saturdays and recommend books to one another.
optionExplanations: 正确：这些活动有助于吸引孩子参与，也与后来访客逐渐增加相呼应。
无中生有：文章没有提到当天归还要求。
无中生有：退休教师帮助整理书籍，故事没有说 Mei 要取代他。
与原文相反：后来家长也开始来图书馆。

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly show?
options: A village library can only succeed with a large budget.
Children learn best when they study alone.
A shared community project can grow from small contributions.
Retired teachers should manage all village activities.
questions.explanation: The library began with a small request and grew through the contributions and participation of villagers.
questions.evidence: Sometimes it begins with an open room, a shared idea, and people willing to help.
optionExplanations: 与原文相反：文章指出社区空间不一定需要大笔预算。
无中生有：文章强调邻里共同参与和学生互相帮助。
正确：概括了小小的起点如何借助大家参与发展成社区项目。
以偏概全：退休教师只帮助整理书籍，并未负责全部活动。

title: A Later Start, A Better Morning?

segments.text: At Green Hill High School, the first bell used to ring at 7:20 a.m. Many students arrived tired, and the first lesson often began quietly. After families raised concerns, the school tested a later start for one term. Classes began thirty minutes later, while dismissal stayed nearly the same.
To make room for the change, the school shortened some passing periods and moved a few activities to lunchtime.
segments.translation: 为了配合时间调整，学校缩短了部分课间时间，并把几项活动移到了午餐时间。

segments.text: Before the trial, students recorded their bedtimes and how alert they felt in the morning. Some simply stayed up later, so they did not feel more rested. Others used the extra time to eat breakfast or travel without rushing. Teachers noted participation in early classes without being told to expect a particular result.

At term's end, many students said waking up was easier, and teachers heard more questions in first-period discussions. But results differed. Students with evening jobs or long bus rides still struggled. Some families also found the later dismissal difficult because of work and childcare.
The trial therefore raised practical questions as well as signs of improvement.
segments.translation: 因此，这次试行既带来了改善的迹象，也提出了一些实际问题。

segments.text: The school has not decided whether to keep the change. It plans to collect information for another term and discuss adjustments with families. The experience suggests that changing a schedule is not simply a matter of moving a clock. A policy affects people differently, so listening to them helps the school decide whether it truly works.

questions.stem: What change did Green Hill High School test?
options: It began classes thirty minutes later.
It ended the school day two hours earlier.
It removed all lunchtime activities.
It made the first lesson optional.
questions.explanation: The trial moved the beginning of classes thirty minutes later and kept the dismissal time nearly the same.
questions.evidence: Classes began thirty minutes later, while dismissal stayed nearly the same.
optionExplanations: 正确：这是学校试行的主要时间调整。
偷换信息：文章说放学时间基本不变，并非提前两小时。
与原文相反：学校只是把几项活动移到午餐时间，并没有取消所有活动。
无中生有：文章没有说第一节课变成选修或可不参加。

questions.stem: Why did some students still feel tired during the trial?
options: The school removed breakfast from the schedule.
They changed their bedtime to a later hour.
Teachers gave them extra homework every morning.
The first bell rang earlier than before.
questions.explanation: Some students used the later start to stay up later, which reduced the possible benefit of additional morning sleep.
questions.evidence: Some simply stayed up later, so they did not feel more rested.
optionExplanations: 无中生有：文章没有说学校取消早餐。
正确：熬夜时间随上课时间推迟，学生并未因此休息得更多。
无中生有：文章没有提到早晨作业增加。
与原文相反：上课开始时间推迟了。

questions.stem: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Every school should copy Green Hill's schedule immediately.
A schedule change may help some people, but schools should consider different needs before deciding.
Students should be responsible for solving all transport problems.
Later school starts always improve every student's learning.
questions.explanation: The trial showed possible benefits as well as difficulties for different students and families, so the school plans to gather more information before deciding.
questions.evidence: A policy affects people differently, so listening to them helps the school decide whether it truly works.
optionExplanations: 过度推断：文章没有建议所有学校立即照搬。
正确：概括了试行结果不一，以及制定政策时要听取不同群体意见。
偷换话题：交通只是部分学生的困难之一，不是文章主旨。
与原文相反：文章说明改善并非对所有人都一样，也提出了实际困难。
